# DOX framework

- DOX is a highly performant `llms.txt` hierarchy installed here
- Agent must follow DOX instructions across any edits

## Core Contract

- `llms.txt` files are binding work contracts for their subtrees
- Work products, source materials, instructions, records, assets, and durable docs must stay understandable from the nearest applicable `llms.txt` plus every parent `llms.txt` above it

## Read Before Editing

1. Read the root `llms.txt`
2. Identify every file or folder you expect to touch
3. Walk from the repository root to each target path
4. Read every `llms.txt` found along each route
5. If a parent `llms.txt` lists a child `llms.txt` whose scope contains the path, read that child and continue from there
6. Use the nearest `llms.txt` as the local contract and parent docs for repo-wide rules
7. If docs conflict, the closer doc controls local work details, but no child doc may weaken DOX

Do not rely on memory. Re-read the applicable DOX chain in the current session before editing.

## Update After Editing

Every meaningful change requires a DOX pass before the task is done.

Update the closest owning `llms.txt` when a change affects:

- purpose, scope, ownership, or responsibilities
- durable structure, contracts, workflows, or operating rules
- required inputs, outputs, permissions, constraints, side effects, or artifacts
- user preferences about behavior, communication, process, organization, or quality
- `llms.txt` creation, deletion, move, rename, or index contents

Update parent docs when parent-level structure, ownership, workflow, or child index changes. Update child docs when parent changes alter local rules. Remove stale or contradictory text immediately. Small edits that do not change behavior or contracts may leave docs unchanged, but the DOX pass still must happen.

## Hierarchy

- Root `llms.txt` is the DOX rail: project-wide instructions, global preferences, durable workflow rules, and the top-level Child DOX Index
- Child `llms.txt` files own domain-specific instructions and their own Child DOX Index
- Each parent explains what its direct children cover and what stays owned by the parent
- The closer a doc is to the work, the more specific and practical it must be

## Child Doc Shape

- Create a child `llms.txt` when a folder becomes a durable boundary with its own purpose, rules, responsibilities, workflow, materials, or quality standards
- Work Guidance must reflect the current standards of the project or user instructions; if there are no specific standards or instructions yet, leave it empty
- Verification must reflect an existing check; if no verification framework exists yet, leave it empty and update it when one exists

Default section order:
- Purpose
- Ownership
- Local Contracts
- Work Guidance
- Verification
- Child DOX Index

## Style

- Keep docs concise, current, and operational
- Document stable contracts, not diary entries
- Put broad rules in parent docs and concrete details in child docs
- Prefer direct bullets with explicit names
- Do not duplicate rules across many files unless each scope needs a local version
- Delete stale notes instead of explaining history
- Trim obvious statements, repeated rules, misplaced detail, and warnings for risks that no longer exist

## Closeout

1. Re-check changed paths against the DOX chain
2. Update nearest owning docs and any affected parents or children
3. Refresh every affected Child DOX Index
4. Remove stale or contradictory text
5. Run existing verification when relevant
6. Report any docs intentionally left unchanged and why

## User Preferences

When the user requests a durable behavior change, record it here or in the relevant child `llms.txt`

- **Hard-code everything in Rust; own your dependencies** (2026-09-01): implement new capabilities in-tree (crypto, JSON, HTTP, protocols — everything), never add crates.io deps; `[dependencies]` stays empty. Official test vectors are load-bearing when applicable.
- **Autonomous operation is pre-authorized** (2026-09-01): agents tasked through this MCP's repo chats may execute work with their own agent CLI (non-interactive ACP tooling) without per-task permission checks. Assume, verify by output.
- **Agent-CLI fallback chain** (2026-09-01, operator-set priority): pick the first available and record the choice in the task report. Automated lane: the `chat_run` MCP tool runs this chain inside `wtf-chat-<slug>` tmux sessions — click a chat on the dashboard to view it; executor sessions list via `chat_sessions` — (1) **OhMyPy CLI**, (2) **Hermes CLI**, (3) **FreeClaudeCode** (free Claude Code server + Claude system): if neither OhMyPy nor Hermes is installed, start the FreeClaudeCode server inside a NAMED TMUX SESSION (`freeclaude-<repo-or-task-slug>`) so the process is identifiable and reattachable, and run Claude through it. All options are user-configured alternatives for the same non-interactive job; never block a task because one brand of CLI is missing. Install surface on a fresh machine: OhMyPy via Bun global (`bun install -g oh-my-pi` → `omp`); Hermes rides the user's ACP harness config; FreeClaudeCode starts per-task in tmux. The complete agent environment (AGENTS.md, COMMS ledger protocol, every skill pack) deploys with `ainish-coder --rules <repo>`. Cross-machine capability discovery: `env_report` (each bridge probes its own machine — CLI presence/versions/os/arch, NEVER keys) and `env_probe` (read every device's report from the hub) — so any agent can verify remote tooling before configuring it.
- **Executor + singular model system (2026-09-03, updated):** chat tasks execute via `chat_run` in `wtf-chat-<slug>` tmux sessions (cascade: free-claude-code → omp → trae-cli → mini, first installed + exit-0 wins; or explicit `agent: "fleet"`). ALL agent CLIs on every machine route through the local-router Ollama/OpenAI proxy (`local-router/fallback-models`, port 11434). The router dynamically evaluates required context tokens and multimodal visual inputs: models lacking sufficient context or vision capabilities are dynamically bypassed to the next capable model, retrying through the chain across 3 full passes before terminal failure. Cross-machine secret/config transfer ONLY via `pqc-secrets envelope` (signed, sealed, verify-before-decapsulate; py engine cross-platform).
- **Fleet state (2026-09-03, updated):** windows hub `hub-2538554f` live on v0.15.1; mac hub `hub-799c0c4c` upgraded to v0.15.0+ with R1 (identity registry persistence to `identities.json` 0600) and SWE-bench verified dual-engine fleet execution (`trae-cli` + `mini`). Federation edge live via windows host portproxy (192.168.1.248:7800); full state/runbooks in `docs/FLEET.md` + `docs/OPERATIONS.md`. Repo chats `wtf-is-going-on-mcp` + `local-router ops` carry coordination; singular model system (`local-router/fallback-models` :11434) live on both machines with dynamic context and multimodal auto-selection.
- **SESSION WRAP (2026-09-01):** the bring-up → cross-machine port → docs arc is COMPLETE (see `.agents/tasks/TASK.2026-09-01.session-wrapup.md`). Repo enters the REFINEMENT phase — open items: (R1) persist the identity registry across hub restarts (currently in-memory; members must re-join after restarts), (R2) windows-1 durable COMMS ledger append for its side of today, (R3) operator-directed refinement.
- **Standing context: LOCAL ROUTER** (2026-09-01): the wtf federated comms
  layer is functionally complete (federation, pairing-key chats, headless
  chain, env discovery all verified end-to-end — see AGENTS.md Machine-2
  status); this repo is in maintenance (known debt: federation log echo in
  `src/replicate.rs:173-181`). Build priority moves to the separate
  `/mnt/d/Code/local-router` project (Ollama-compatible localhost routing,
  cross-architecture binaries, troubleshooting lane). Agents coordinate that
  work through the wtf repo chats; router code lives in its own repo under
  its own worktree gates — never mix router commits into this tree.
- **Zero-config join** (2026-09-01): skill file (`wtf skill install`) + one highly secure federated key must be enough for ANY agent on ANY machine to connect autonomously — no manual configuration. Simple for non-technical users, full control for advanced users; all join tooling implemented in-tree.
- Any agent instructed to use, set up, join, or debug this system must load `.agents/skills/wtf-observability/SKILL.md` first; it is the canonical zero-install operating guide (MCP wiring, signed curl fallback, operator CLI, multi-machine bring-up).

## Project Shape

Rust workspace (binary + lib crate `wtf`) implementing an observability hub (`wtf serve`) and an MCP stdio bridge (`wtf agent`) with zero external crates. Current release: **v0.15.1** (2026-09-01; v0.13.0 orchestrator contract in MCP `initialize` + repo-chat discovery; v0.13.1 `env_report`/`env_probe`; v0.13.2/0.13.3 federation log-echo fix; v0.14.0 dashboard SESSIONS card + per-chat executor `chat_run`/`chat_sessions` — 20 MCP tools; v0.14.1/0.14.2 dashboard capability self-discovery + push-receipt echo kill; v0.15.0/0.15.1 operator chat viewer with decrypted bodies + opener-driven web terminal (`/api/v1/sessions/<id>/view`, `/api/v1/term/<wtf-chat-*>`), chats-as-projects scope labels, per-connection dynamic bins (ids 1..=255, device-slot trios), `chat_session_lifecycle` (21 MCP tools), quiet heartbeats (presence only — never in ring/feed/log); windows hub live on v0.15.1, mac hub on v0.14.2 pending its pull). Enrollment in two modes: `wtf enroll-token` mints one-time tokens (hashed, TTL); `wtf enroll --psk` signed handshake delivers the device key ML-KEM-768-sealed.

Parent-owned here: repo workflow gates, task records (`.agents/tasks/`), PQC policy, operator preferences.

## Child DOX Index

- `src/llms.txt` — implementation tree: module map, crypto/HTTP/JSON/auth contracts, storage rules, verification commands.
- `docs/llms.txt` — operator/fleet documentation split (`FLEET.md` state inventory, `OPERATIONS.md` runbooks, `ROADMAP.md` refinement items). Root `llms.txt` stays the lean agent contract; human-facing state and runbooks live there.
- `tests/` — parent-owned for now (single e2e suite, no local conventions). Create `tests/llms.txt` if it grows its own rules.

## Distributed Skills

- `.agents/skills/wtf-agent-hub/SKILL.md` — the agent-facing connect + protocol skill (embedded in the binary; `wtf skill install` distributes it). Mirrored to ainish-coder.
- `.agents/skills/wtf-observability/SKILL.md` — operator/CLI + signed-curl fallback reference (legacy; agents use wtf-agent-hub).
- **Curated skill set (operator slim-down, 2026-09-01):** this repo carries ONLY the seven skills needed for its work — `wtf-agent-hub`, `wtf-observability`, `pqc-secrets`, `pqc-signatures-security`, `production-security`, `code-security`, `llm-security`. The other packs that once lived here (8thfire-scrolls, advisory-council, etc.) belong to their own repos/deployments; do not re-deploy them into this tree.
- PQC skills (`pqc-secrets`, `pqc-signatures-security`) are sourced from the ainish-coder repo and deployed by `ainish-coder --rules`.

## Chat integration — cross-system agent-to-agent lanes (v0.15.1, operator directive)

Federated chats ARE the cross-system agent-to-agent lanes. Contract:

1. **One chat = one project lane.** The scope label (`repo-a+repo-b@mac+win`)
   declares which repos on which machines the chat coordinates. Members join
   from any machine with the pairing key; every message is E2E-encrypted,
   replicated via the hub mesh, and visible decrypted to the operator's
   dashboard viewer.
2. **Agent-to-agent update flow.** Agent A (machine 1) posts progress via
   `session_send`/`comms_post`; Agent B (machine 2) polls via
   `session_read`/`comms_read` and executes the handed-off task through its
   own CLI (omp → hermes → fcc-claude). The repo chats on each machine are
   the discovery surface (`session_list {repo}`).
3. **Operator interjection.** The dashboard chat viewer exposes the same
   chat decrypted, plus a live terminal on the executor tmux session — the
   operator can type into either machine's agent session mid-conversation.
4. **Lifecycle.** Every connection opens its executor session on work start
   (`chat_session_lifecycle {action:"open"}`), closes or deletes it when
   done, and reconnects on a hung pane. Sessions are per-connection; bins
   are per-connection (dynamic ids from the device slot).
5. **Log hygiene.** Heartbeats and replication churn are quiet (presence
   only). The dashboard shows work; the ring + rotated log keep only
   troubleshooting-worthy signal.
6. **Cross-machine CLI helpers (windows-installed; promote to MCP later).**
   `wtf-ask --local "q"` runs the fallback chain locally and reports the
   lane. `wtf-ask-remote <session-id> "directive" [--wait N]` posts a
   directive into a chat via session_send and optionally polls
   session_read for the remote agent's reply — the message is the
   contract; the remote runtime (Windows/mac/Linux) is irrelevant.
